senses.gloss:
Nakha denotes either the ‘nail’ of a man,^1 or the ‘claw’ of
a wild beast, such as a tiger.^2 The trimming (nikṛntana)^3 of
the nails was a regular part of the toilet of the Vedic Indian,
especially on occasions of special sanctity, when it accompanied
the cleansing of the teeth.^4
1) Rv. i. 162, 9; x. 163, 5; Av. ii. 33,
6, etc.
2) Rv. iv. 3, 3. Cf. x. 28, 10, of the
eagle's talon.
3) Chāndogya Upaniṣad, vi. 1, 6.
4) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, ii. 5, 1, 7;
Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 6, 2, etc.;
Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, ii. 1, 3, 4.
